purpose: Adefovir dipivoxil is used to treat chronic hepatitis B, which is a long-term viral infection that affects your liver. It helps slow down the virus so your liver stays healthier. It is used in adults and sometimes in children over 12 years old.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking a key tool the hepatitis B virus uses to make copies of itself inside your body. Think of it like throwing a wrench into the virus's copy machine — it slows the virus down so it cannot spread as easily. Over time, this helps reduce damage to your liver.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include weakness or tiredness, stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, and headache. Some people may also notice mild stomach pain or gas. These side effects are often manageable, so let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: This medication can affect your kidneys, especially if taken for a long time or at higher doses, so your doctor will regularly check your kidney function with blood tests. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, because stopping abruptly can cause the hepatitis B virus to flare up and seriously harm your liver. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems before starting this medicine, and avoid taking it with other medications that can also affect the kidneys.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults and children over 12 years old is one 10 mg tablet taken by mouth once daily. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
